selection_basis: Training + validation participants only (seed 13). No outer test fold was inspected before this configuration was frozen.

window_length_decision.rule: Choose the window length that scores best on validation participants.
window_length_decision.evidence: 20 s outperformed 10 s and 5 s at EVERY delay candidate: all four 20 s configurations scored above every 10 s and 5 s configuration in the 3-fold sweep. The ordering 20 s > 10 s > 5 s was consistent, so the effect is treated as real.
window_length_decision.note: Stride is held fixed at 5 s across all candidates so that every window length yields predictions at the same temporal resolution; overlap therefore varies (75% at 20 s, 50% at 10 s, 0% at 5 s). Because splits are grouped by participant, overlapping windows cannot cross the train/test boundary.

annotation_delay_decision.rule: Pre-declared: if delay optimisation does not provide a STABLE improvement across validation folds, use zero shift and state this transparently.
annotation_delay_decision.evidence: In the 3-fold sweep the delay optimum was inconsistent across window lengths (best at 1 s for 5 s windows, 2 s for 10 s windows, 3 s for 20 s windows), the signature of noise-chasing rather than a consistent physiological lag. A confirmation run at 20 s using ALL FIVE validation folds shrank the delay-3 advantage from +0.027 to +0.008 mean CCC (0.2411 +/- 0.0567 versus 0.2334 +/- 0.0521), an order of magnitude smaller than the fold-to-fold standard deviation.
annotation_delay_decision.transparency_note: The 3-fold argmax would have selected a 3 s delay. It was rejected after the 5-fold confirmation showed the advantage was not stable. This is reported in the manuscript rather than silently adopting the larger number.
